items.title: Disney Admits Live-Action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu  'Underperformed', But Says The Movies Still Helped Shift Plenty of Merchandise
items.description: Disney's live-action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu both underperformed at the box office, but their ticket sales are only part of the story, the company has argued.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney's live-action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu both underperformed at the box office, but their ticket sales are only part of the story, the company has argued.

As part of its latest financial results, Disney admitted that both Moana and The Mandalorian and Grogu's theatrical revenues had been disappointing, but said that both movies had made up for this to some degree by also shifting plenty of merchandise.

Moana is currently languishing on a $263 million box office, against a $250 million budget, making it almost as bad a box office bomb as the widely-panned live-action Snow White. Factoring in additional marketing costs, the film will not have turned a profit. Sentiment towards the film was not positive ahead of time, with many fans questioning why the project even existed (while others were too busy creating memes featuring The Rock's wig).

The Mandalorian and Grogu, meanwhile, finished its theatrical run on a box office of $345 million against a $165 million budget. While this is a better profit margin than Moana, it is still the lowest box office for any live-action Star Wars film — even Solo. Still, Disney is keen to tell shareholders that ticket sales are only one metric to measure these movies' success.

"These franchise investments contributed to value creation beyond their theatrical releases," Disney said in its financial earnings. In particular, Mandalorian and Grogu "drove healthy growth in retail sales for the Star Wars franchise during the quarter," Disney continued.

"Looking ahead, we expect the live-action Moana to be a strong title on Disney+, building on the success of the original film, which is one of the most streamed movies of all time, and extending the reach of the franchise, which now includes three films, a themed area at EPCOT, and a robust global merchandise business."

Still, despite this positive spin, the chances of a live-action Moana 2 seem slim-to-none. As for the Mandalorian and his young ward, there's no word yet of when or where these characters might appear again. (Upcoming Disney+ series Ahsoka is expected to lay the final pieces of groundwork for an Heir to the Empire project featuring Thrawn, though Dave Filoni's long-promised team-up project currently remains uncertain.)

Elsewhere, Disney celebrated the $1 billion box office success of Toy Story 5, and said that The Devil Wears Prada 2 had also performed well, particularly internationally. Today also marked the announcement of a new initiative to fill Disney+ with user-made TikTok content, which seems to replace the company's earlier plans to flood its streaming platform with AI slop videos made using Sora.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Pokémon Pokopia Version 2.0.0 Released, And Here Are the Full Patch Notes
items.description: Nintendo Switch 2 hit Pokémon Pokopia has received its big Version 2.0.0 update, adding a bunch of free content, support for its Bubbly Basin expansion, and much more.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo Switch 2 hit Pokémon Pokopia has received its big Version 2.0.0 update, adding a bunch of free content, support for its Bubbly Basin expansion, and much more.

Today's patch is now live on Switch 2 for all Pokémon Pokopia owners, whether you have the game's Expansion Pass or not. As previously announced, all players will get the ability to survive and build underwater for the first time, thanks to the all-new Dive ability. This adds a cute bubble to your Ditto character's head, finally allowing them to survive beneath the waves for more than a few seconds.

All players can now access an array of new recipes, emotes, hair colors, and more, while the patch notes below list out some useful gameplay improvements. As well as changes to make locating Pokémon more straightforward, you'll now be able to perform various actions multiple times in the same interaction, and appraise up to 10 relics at the same time.

Of course, players who own Pokopia's Expansion Pass will also now be able to access its Bubbly Basin DLC. You'll just need to have learnt the new Dive move and upgraded Bleak Beach's Raise the Environment Level quest to level 5. After that, Popplio will appear at the area's Pokémon Center, and guide you to the new Bubbly Basin gate.

Today's full patch notes lie below:

Pokémon Pokopia: Ver. 2.0.0

The following features have been added:

  • Added the move Dive, allowing players to move freely underwater.
  • The Build specialty can now be used to build houses underwater.
  • Added new items such as the portal pod and safe.
    • Recipes can be purchased after increasing Palette Town’s environment level.
  • Added the new pattern, dynamic Ditto print.
    • Can be obtained by talking to Smearguru after acquiring the diploma.
  • Added new emotes: Lie Down and Ready, Set, Go!
    • Can be obtained in Bleak Beach and on Dream Islands.
  • Added five new hair colors: orange, light pink, yellow-green, blue-green, and brown.
  • Added a function to move items in bulk between the storage box and bag.
  • Added a function to delete items placed inside objects such as the garbage bin.
  • Added the ability to fine-tune depth placement when placing windows, doors, and similar items.
  • Added an option in Settings to hide the confirmation message shown when canceling Magnet Rise.
  • Added an option in Settings allowing movement while the move wheel is open.
  • Added motion-sickness reduction settings for the camera.
  • The following items can now be painted: stylish stool, handrail, metal chain, workbench, vending machine, bike, bookcase, Pokémon Center counter, arrow sign, rope.

The following improvements have been implemented:

  • Even if a Pokémon’s habitat is destroyed, it will move back in if the same habitat is rebuilt within a certain area.
  • Pokémon that are sad because furniture was removed will now notice more quickly when the same furniture is replaced.
  • Pokémon that taught you an emote will now respond with the same emote when you use it.
  • If a Pokémon being searched for in the Pokédex is in another town, you can now travel to that town using Return Home.
  • Reduced ordinary conversation indicators so that special Pokémon conversations and requests directed at Ditto stand out more clearly.
  • Lost relics can now be appraised in batches of up to 10 at a time.
  • Paint, Gather Honey, and Collect can now be performed multiple times in the same interaction.
  • During crafting, materials in the storage box next to the workbench will be consumed before materials in the bag.
  • Increased the placement limit for power generators (excluding furnaces) from 64 to 128.
  • Increased the number of different photos that can be displayed in a town from 10 to 40.
  • When sucking up liquid, a short press of the move button to hold liquids in Ditto’s mouth will allow liquid to be held in their mouth without removing it from the environment.
  • When releasing stored water, adjusted water levels now automatically match nearby water levels.
  • Smearguru can now learn patterns from photos stored in References.
  • Improved visibility of the target item when painting with paint balloons.
  • Increased the amount of treasure discoverable with the Dowsing Machine on Dream Islands.
  • Pokémon companions can now follow you while moving with Surf, Glide, Rollout, or Magnet Rise.
  • Inhaling items and opening the bag are now possible while rolling using Rollout.
  • Rollout can now destroy certain natural objects such as large boulders.
  • Surf can now be activated on land by pressing the Surf button while holding the focus button.
  • Improved activation conditions for Surf and Waterfall so they occur more smoothly.
  • Leafage can now be used on farm soil to revert it to a normal soil block.
  • Strength can now be used underwater.
  • Added an All tab to both the Pokédex and Habitat Dex.
  • Made it clearer that buildings can still be remodeled even when items such as the Ditto Flag are attached to roofs or walls.
  • During construction, any Pokémon not assigned to the Build role in a building project can now help with cooking.
  • Prevented treasures in Sparkling Skylands from appearing when using the Dowsing Machine in locations where breaking terrain would cause them to fall.
  • Improved messaging when there are insufficient materials for copying items using the 3D Printer.
  • Items can now be placed on top of square plants.
  • Hide-and-sneak can now be canceled midway.
  • Adjusted in-game event notifications shown at startup so they are displayed only during specific remaining-day periods.
  • Certain roof items now block water.
  • Increased output when crafting curved eaves to 10.
  • Tidal Bell and Clear Bell can now be triggered using laser sensors and switches.
  • Adjusted sound effects for camping chair and sleeping bag.
  • Improved performance for certain rendering processes.

The following issues have been fixed:

  • When talking to a Pokémon that is currently assigned to construct buildings, options such as “Follow me!” may sometimes fail to appear.
  • Suicune and Gholdengo may be unable to travel across water.
  • Pokémon may occasionally fall into the ocean or off cliffs when appearing from their habitats.
  • Even when using honey, Pokémon may sometimes fail to return to their habitats.
  • Using Magnet Rise may occasionally cause Pokémon to scold or warn the player.
  • Pokémon that dislike water may sometimes be unable to move across duckweed and flowering duckweed on the water’s surface.
  • Requests from Pokémon may occasionally ask for items that the requesting Pokémon actually dislikes.
  • When processing berries in the community box, paint may not be produced correctly.
  • The timing of the note played by the music mat (high Do) is offset incorrectly.
  • Certain furniture can be painted through specific procedures even on parts where the colors are not actually changeable.
  • Painting certain items may use more paint than intended.
  • The light color of a painted surface light may fail to change correctly.
  • Under specific conditions, it is possible to place more than one party cooking pot in the same town.
  • Some items may display unnaturally when viewed from a distance.
  • For some items, visual effects may disappear when viewed through glass.
  • Under certain conditions during multiplayer, building may become impossible to complete or cancel.
  • In certain situations, it may be unclear why actions such as building or relocation cannot be performed.
  • On Cloud Islands, players other than the administrator may be able to place a relocation kit.
  • Under certain conditions, a building kit may become unrecoverable when remodeling a house.
  • Under certain conditions, painted portions of the sand house may be reset.
  • Using Rock Smash while falling may cause Ditto’s position or height to become significantly displaced.
  • During the Withered Wasteland request “Clear the path!” Slowpoke may stop moving partway through.
  • During the Sparkling Skylands request “Follow Tinkmaster!” certain actions may prevent the request from progressing.
  • During the Sparkling Skylands request “Pokémon Center tour guide!” searching for Tinkmaster in the Pokédex may guide the player to the town containing their habitat rather than the town where they are currently located.
  • Loading may occasionally fail to finish when returning from a Dream Island.
  • Returning from a Dream Island may incorrectly send the player to Palette Town.
  • Under certain conditions when an online session ends, the player may be transported to a Dream Island.
  • On the Cloud Island loading screen, the player’s gender pronoun may sometimes be displayed incorrectly in some languages.

We have made several additional adjustments and fixed a number of bugs to improve the overall gameplay experience.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Disney+ Announces Plans to Feature User-Made TikTok Content, Just Days After Emmy-Nominated Wonder Man Cancellation
items.description: Disney's streaming service will soon feature user-made content from TikTok, the company has announced.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney's streaming service will soon feature user-made content from TikTok, the company has announced.

Described as a "first-of-its-kind global deal" that will open doors "for the next generation of creators," the partnership will see Disney-related fan content from TikTok added to Disney+ in the form of "Verts" — short-form vertical videos.

Disney has said it will allow creators access to hundreds of films and series in its back catalogue in return for them pumping out videos that touch on Disney brands, including Star Wars, Marvel, Pixar and shows on FX. The exact guidelines here are unclear, however, and Disney has said it will "thoughtfully curate" the videos it picks to highlight. So, don't expect to see too many Verts criticizing Rise of Skywalker.

In a nutshell, Disney+ gets to add content it has paid next to nothing for, while content creators potentially get their work seen by an enormous audience. It sounds like a great business decision for both sides, though today's announcement will hardly install confidence in the platform's future quality bar — especially just days after the shock cancellation of Emmy-nominated series Wonder Man.

"The best storytellers are fans first," said Asad Ayaz, Chief Marketing and Brand Officer, The Walt Disney Company in a statement. "That has always been true at Disney, and today, fans are celebrating our stories in entirely new ways. This collaboration creates a new bridge between the stories we tell and the creativity they inspire, giving creators a bigger stage to share what they’ve made, and audiences more to discover on Disney+ every day."

Today's announcement comes just months after the abrupt cancellation of Disney's previous push to fill its streaming service with user-made short-form content, via a deal with OpenAI. That partnership would have seen Disney pay $1 billion for the privilege of having 100 of its most beloved characters thrown into OpenAI's Sora video slop engine for users to generate content from. However, the whole thing collapsed after OpenAI ditched Sora, and decided it could make more money elsewhere.

Image credit: Disney

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: 'It Seems a Little Open-Ended': Spider-Man: Brand New Day's Jacob Batalon Discusses The Movie's Big Moment Between Peter and Ned
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day actor Jacob Batalon has discussed his interpretation for the movie's big final moment between Peter and Ned.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day actor Jacob Batalon has discussed his interpretation for the movie's big final moment between Peter and Ned.

Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow...

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Batalon was asked about his final scene with Tom Holland, and whether their characters' handshake suggested that Ned's memories of Peter had been restored.

While Batalon stopped short of providing an official confirmation, the actor said that Ned remembering his secret handshake with Peter implied "a slight glint or little glimmer" of recognition had returned.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day picks up the action some five years after Spider-Man: No Way Home, which concluded with Ned, MJ and the rest of the world all forgetting who Spider-Man's real identity was. Years on, Brand New Day confirms that Ned and MJ still don't remember Peter at all, despite the latter finding Peter's letter he wrote to her professing his love.

That said, there are clues that the characters do still remember something of Peter, even subconsciously so. In the scene where Peter hangs out with Ned and MJ in their flat, MJ draws Spider-Man in his Homecoming suit, and at the end of the film, MJ is back on the rooftop she previously visited with Peter, holding the necklace that Peter gave her.

Fans have various theories for what's going on, from Ned and MJ's interactions beginning to unlock their memories naturally, to the effects of Jean Grey's forcefield giving their memories a nudge.

Another clue here seems to come from the Hulk, who said that being possessed by Jean had the effect of unlocking something that had been kept behind a barrier. It's suggested that Hulk also remembers Peter, which is potentially why he lets Spider-Man go and lets himself fall from the building instead.

All of which takes to that handshake with Ned, which Batalon says has been left "a little open-ended."

"What if it’s just muscle memory? What if he just remembers that handshake but nothing else about Peter? What if he just repeats 'Peter' because that’s what Peter says his name is in that moment? I don’t know," Batalon said.

"I feel like it’s really up to interpretation for everyone. There could be a slight glint or little glimmer [of recognition], if you will."

As part of the same interview, Batalon was also asked about Brand New Day's post-credits scene, which features the Spidey Tracker app that Ned built. Unfortunately, Batalon seemed completely in the dark on this. "You think me, of all people, knows top-brass-level information?" he responded. "Come on."

Will MJ and Ned have their memories of Peter fully restored? This is likely something we'll see explored in the inevitable Spider-Man 5, which seems certain now that Brand New Day has done so well at the box office. Indeed, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has noted that there are plans for more Spidey adventures and Holland has said he's keen to help eventually introduce Miles Morales into the MCU.

Image credit: Eric Charbonneau/Sony Pictures via Getty Images

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: With Avatar's Future Still Uncertain, James Cameron Now Says He Wants to Prioritize 'Other Stories' For the 'Last Act' of His Career
items.description: Avatar director James Cameron has signaled that he may be ready to move on from the franchise, as the status of its two planned sequels still remains uncertain.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Avatar director James Cameron has signaled that he may be ready to move on from the franchise, as the status of its two planned sequels remains uncertain.

Disney has pencilled in release dates for an Avatar 4 and Avatar 5 over the next five years, but has yet to give the greenlight for production to start. And there are questions over how well these films will perform financially after the waning — but admittedly still enormous — returns for 2025's Avatar: Fire and Ash.

Last year's movie earned $1.4 billion at the box office, a remarkable amount for any film, but around half the money made by the first Avatar ($2.9 billion), and nearly a billion less than Avatar: The Way of Water ($2.3 billion). At the same time, Avatar films are incredibly costly to produce, meaning that they need to earn huge amounts to turn a profit.

With Avatar's future unclear, Cameron has discussed the need to prioritize "other stories" that he wanted to see made during the "last act" of his career. The 71-year-old filmmaker has long had various other ideas for films other than Avatar sequels, though has not directed a non-Avatar blockbuster since 1997's Titanic.

"That's the question of the hour for me," Cameron said in an interview following his receipt of a prestigious Canadian arts award. "There's been momentum in the Avatar universe for 21 years at this point because we started in 2005. I took a little time off to build a submersible and dive to the deepest spot on the planet, as you do, but I came back to Avatar after that. And it's been kind of an unbroken continuum.

"So this is the point where I'm looking at the landscape and asking, 'What are the other stories I want to tell? How many of them do I need to direct myself versus writing and/or producing with other filmmakers?'" he continued.

What are these other stories? Cameron has long discussed adapting Ghosts of Hiroshima, which focuses on the story of a man who survived both bombs that dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in World War 2. Cameron first discussed the project back in 2010 and has continued to show interest, and in 2024 said he hoped he would shoot the film last year (something that did not happen). Other ideas that Cameron has previously discussed include an adaptation of Joe Abercrombie’s dark fantasy book The Devils, plus Terminator and Alita: Battle Angel sequels. Which of these Cameron is considering shooting first, however, remains unclear.

"The criterion — I've literally mapped this out for myself over the last two weeks — I started with, 'What will do the most good?' I put that in block letters at the top," Cameron continued. "And I started looking at all the projects I'm most fond of, asking, 'How's this going to improve our condition? How's that going to make the world better for our kids?'

"I haven't made those decisions yet. I'm still in this liminal state of mapping out... the last act, if you will. And I don't know if that last act will last a year or 20 years."

In April, an update from producer Rae Sanchini stated that the scripts for Avatar 4 and 5 were in hand as the franchise's team continued to move "full speed ahead." But in May, Cameron said he was "looking at some new technologies" to try and get Avatar 4 and 5 made "in half the time for two-thirds of the cost," something that would need to take a year just to figure it out.

Disney has currently scheduled tentative release dates of December 21, 2029 for Avatar 4 and December 19, 2031 for Avatar 5 — but, again, these are just placeholders until plans are made concrete.

items.title: Original Grand Tour Hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May Will Cameo in the New Season
items.description: The original former Top Gear trio set to make appearances alongside their replacements in the returning series.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
The Grand Tour co-creator Andy Wilman has confirmed that original hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May will be making cameo appearances in the new season, alongside their replacements. Wilman revealed the plan with 3Bs radio at the Buckingham Literary Festival, via The Independent.

“We’ve got three guys coming soon with a new Grand Tour and we’ve got behind them,” said Wilman. “We’re really supporting them.”

“Our guys are in the shows doing cameos, so we’re wishing them well because we do want to pass that baton on.”

Wilman co-created The Grand Tour with Clarkson, Hammond, and May for Prime Video, and it premiered in late 2016. The show was established after Wilman, Hammond, and May departed the BBC in the wake of Clarkson’s suspension and subsequent sacking from the hugely popular Top Gear. Well over a decade prior, Wilman and Clarkson co-created the revived version of Top Gear that we know today, which debuted in 2002.

The Grand Tour officially revealed its new host line-up back in February, which consists of motoring journalists Thomas Holland and James Engelsman – an existing duo from successful motoring YouTube channel Throttle House – and trainspotting UK social media personality Francis Bourgeois. It was recently confirmed that the new six-episode season will arrive on Prime this September.

While limited to cameos, the involvement of Clarkson, Hammond, and May does position The Grand Tour rather differently to Top Gear, which went through a revolving line-up of hosts after the original trio left – to mixed critic and audience reactions. Top Gear saw eight different hosts from 2016 up until the show was put on ice in 2023.

items.title: Joke Game Priced at 200 Dollars Rakes In $1.3 Million on Steam Before Thousands of Players Refund It
items.description: The teenaged developer of a joke game titled This Game Costs 200 Dollars almost made over $1 million before thousands of players refunded it.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The teenaged developer of a joke game titled This Game Costs 200 Dollars almost made over $1 million before thousands of players refunded it.

18-year-old Michael Major is behind the viral game, which is actually a sequel to his previous title, This Game Costs 10 Dollars. Major said he created the game as a simple joke, figuring no one would actually buy it due to its exorbitant price, which is the maximum amount of money that developers can charge on the Steam.

In fact, the Steam page’s ‘About This Game’ section describes it as “the swindle to end all swindles,” with Major writing, “I know some people will buy this game out of sheer curiosity, and I highly recommend you do, too.”

Little did he expect that thousands of players would actually take him up on his offer. As reported by local New Hampshire news outlet WMUR-TV, Major’s simplistic, top-down game raked in $1,345,650… sort of.

As shown by Major’s Steam Works Sales and Activations Report, a total of 6,717 units were sold, with 6,705 of those purchases originating in China. Four were sold within the United States, three in Hong Kong, two in Spain, and one each in Saudi Arabia, Taiwan, and Singapore. Most of these buyers returned the game without even playing it (the average playtime for those who actually did play was around 10 minutes), getting refunds that whittled the impressive $1.3 million figure down to a measly $2,045.

“They might be buying it to return it instantly so they can get some kind of points for the highest amount possible without actually paying $200,” Major speculated, referencing Steam Points, which are rewards that players accrue with each purchase that can be used to snag profile swag and other customization goodies. Steam also allows users to refund any game within 14 days of purchase and less than two hours of total playtime, something these buyers clearly took advantage of.

Major theorized that his prank game could have been used to launder funds, saying, “I’m not joking, I have heard of expensive games on Steam being used for money laundering. I have no idea. I could be on a ‘hit list’ right now.”

Speaking to WMUR-TV, Major joked that he “almost died” when he saw the $1.3 million figure in his Steam Report, saying he would have “quit his job” if he’d actually made that much.

On the opposite end of that spectrum, another indie game developer and Twitch streamer broke down in tears after learning that his tower defense game Tangy TD raked in $31,942 just thirty hours after launch, sparking a viral moment that made the game even more popular.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Spider-Man Theory May Change How You See Brand New Day's Ending
items.description: A new Spider-Man: Brand New Day fan theory may help explain the ending of the film.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
This article contains spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day. You've been warned.

A new Spider-Man: Brand New Day fan theory may help explain the ending of the film.

During the climax of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Peter Parker orders Doctor Strange to cast a spell that will make everyone forget about Peter Parker, including his friends and loved ones. It's a powerful moment of self-sacrifice, but one that takes a mental toll on Peter. He's now totally alone; his girlfriend has moved on and has no memory of him, and his best friend has forgotten him.

At the end of Brand New Day, both MJ and Ned appear to be remembering Peter. MJ is seen crying on the rooftop of Midtown High, where the trio would frequently hang out, while also holding on to the necklace Peter gave her. It's not explicitly said, but it seems clear that she is wrestling with her forgotten past in some capacity. However, the more widely-debated scene is the final moment of the film.

Peter reintroduces himself to Ned at a bodega and does their signature handshake, which Ned seems to subconsciously remember. He then exclaims, "Peter!" before it cuts to black. Many viewers believe this signals that the spell is broken for Ned, while others think it's not as cut and dry. However, one TikTok user suggested that there's more magic at play.

@yayaahlyzee he is like part wizard now ?? rewatching the older ones after seeing brand new day and i dont remember that happening . at the end of bnd they do the hand shake , was that enough to give him his memories back ? #spiderman #spidermannowayhome #spidermanbrandnewday #fyp #ned ♬ SPIDER-MAN: Brand New Day - Trailer Music - Ayhan Music

In Spider-Man: No Way Home, Ned and Peter do their handshake after Ned has begun to show signs that he is capable of producing magic using Doctor Strange's sling ring. Later in the film, he conjures portals that introduce the other Spider-Men. Is it possible that the handshake is now charged with magic, and that this, in turn, breaks the spell at the end of Brand New Day? Who's to say! But it's certainly a compelling theory.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Ned's actor, Jacob Batalon, addressed the ending, but wouldn't confirm or deny any theories or implications it may have.

"First and foremost, does Ned actually remember him, though?" asked Batalon. "It seems a little open-ended. What if it’s just muscle memory? What if he just remembers that handshake but nothing else about Peter? What if he just repeats 'Peter' because that’s what Peter says his name is in that moment? I don’t know. I feel like it’s really up to interpretation for everyone. For me, I think it’s a really cool little nod, so hopefully things happen from there."

He went on to suggest that there might be a "a slight glint or little glimmer" of recognition, though.

It's unclear when we will see the next Spider-Man film with Tom Holland. Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has noted that there are plans for more Spidey adventures and Holland sees a long-term plan that will eventually introduce Miles Morales into the MCU. After Brand New Day shattered box office records, it seems difficult to imagine Sony and Marvel will waste much time, but there's nothing officially on the slate yet.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Reportedly Cut a Scene With a Fan-Favorite Daredevil Character And It Might've Fixed a Plot Hole
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day almost had even more MCU cameos, and one of them may have fixed a slight plot hole.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day spoilers are featured in the article below. You've been warned.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day almost had even more MCU cameos, and one of them may have fixed a slight plot hole.

At the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, our beloved wall-crawler jumps in front of a bullet for Jean Grey after The Punisher takes a shot at her. This heroic moment nearly kills him, but he's thankfully rushed to a hospital, with Jean Grey using her powers to keep him alive until doctors stabilize him. However, fans have raised a concern regarding the fact Peter is unmasked in his hospital room, as this would mean there are at least a handful of random people who know his secret identity.

Of course, it's just the nature of the situation, and Peter probably places some trust in the people saving his life. However, there was a cut scene that may have actually helped explain this. According to a post from @JuanEditz on X (who had accurately leaked some details about the film's marketing plans), Claire Temple had a small role in Brand New Day. Rosario Dawson previously confirmed that she reprised her Daredevil role in the film, but didn't reveal the specifics.

there was also another scene cut where the doctors are ripping open his suit but leave his mask on

— juan (@JuanEditzs) August 2, 2026

Now, the X user claims that in a deleted scene, doctors would've cut Peter out of his suit and left his mask on to protect his secret identity. He would've then woken up with his mask still on and then bumped into Claire in the hallway, who was examining an X-Ray. The two would've had a "cute" interaction, and that would've been the end of it. Juan noted that he wasn't sure if Claire was in the room when they cut Spidey's suit off, but speculated that it was certainly possible.

The scene likely would've fixed fan concerns regarding Peter being unmasked by strangers. Claire Temple also likely knows the importance of maintaining a secret identity, since she patched up Daredevil on multiple occasions and has experience with a sensitive matters like this one. As of right now, it's unclear whether Claire will return in a future Marvel project, such as Daredevil: Born Again Season 3.

Nevertheless, none of this actually hurt the movie. Brand New Day just had the biggest domestic opening in history, dethroning Avengers: Endgame. It's also on track to score over $2 billion at the box office and is among some of the best-reviewed Marvel films in history.

items.title: Tom Holland and Zendaya Are On an Unprecedented Box Office Run
items.description: Tom Holland and Zendaya could set some astonishing records this year thanks to Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Tom Holland and Zendaya could set some astonishing records this year thanks to Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey.

The couple just had back-to-back releases that are proving to be box office juggernauts. Spaced only two weeks apart, the duo had key roles in both The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, both of which have or will cross the billion-dollar mark at the box office. Brand New Day is expected to go the distance and make $2 billion, partially assisted by a newly-added IMAX release.

The films have set box office records, with Spider-Man specifically dethroning Avengers: Endgame's biggest domestic opening. In total, both films have officially accumulated nearly $2 billion at the box office and are expected to rack up a lot more money before they leave theaters, possibly bringing the total closer to or in excess of $3 billion.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Reportedly Had a Troubled Development That Impacted a Now-Canceled Multiplayer Project
items.description: A new report suggests that Halo: Campaign Evolved had a fairly troubled development.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A new report suggests that Halo: Campaign Evolved had a fairly troubled development.

According to Rebs Gaming, a popular Halo insider whose reporting journalists have corroborated in the past, the recent Halo remake underwent major changes during its development. Halo Studios works with a bevy of external teams and contractors, something that may have led to issues during Campaign Evolved's development. A studio known as Abstraction was recruited around 2023 to help modify the original game's work and make it compatible with a new engine and new features.

Halo Studios opted to utilize Unreal Engine 5, which created issues since the original game was designed on a rather ancient engine known as Blam. Abstraction worked to gel the two together and make it so new elements like sprinting, four-player co-op, and more all felt organic in Campaign Evolved. The original levels and combat encounters weren't designed for these things, so not accounting for them could have created all kinds of issues.

Unfortunately, Rebs Gaming reportedly discovered that Abstraction was prematurely kicked off the remake after Halo Studios imposed unrealistic deadlines and expectations on a technically complex project. The studio wasn't credited in the game's credits, but individual staff members were given special thanks. A source told Rebs Gaming that Abstraction's work was thrown out and redone quickly, which is believed to have caused bugs and AI problems.

The insider went on to claim that the studio's hubris led to further setbacks down the line. It was believed that the pivot to Unreal Engine 5 would have made things easier, but that wasn't the case. The team was led to believe by leadership that they could port assets into Unreal; instead, 100% of those assets had to reportedly be rebuilt in the engine, which the team didn't account for.

Rebs Gaming went on to allege that overall mismanagement created multiple obstacles for the team and even led to the cancellation of a multiplayer Halo project, as the Campaign Evolved team needed its staff and resources. In the final year of the game's development, the team had to crunch in order to get it out on time.

Additionally, the game was planned to utilize real-time cutscenes, which would've allowed players to see their custom armor and weapons. This unfortunately had to be scrapped, as the external team working on the game's cinematics "struggled" and barely made it in time for release.

Ultimately, Halo: Campaign Evolved is being received fairly well, but it has also left some fans feeling like there was more to be desired with its various issues. It's unclear how the game is selling yet, but we'll likely know within the next few weeks as sales data comes out. The team did tease a Halo 2 remake at the end of this one, so perhaps there is more to come. We can only hope it's not as messy as this game's development, though.

items.title: Oded Fehr Gives First Look at Ardeth Bay in The Mummy 4
items.description: Ardeth Bay is returning in The Mummy 4, as is his original actor Oded Fehr, who gave fans a sneak peek at what the character looks like after all these years.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Ardeth Bay is returning in The Mummy 4, as is his original actor Oded Fehr, who gave fans a sneak peek at what the character looks like after all these years.

Brendan Fraser and co. are making their long-awaited return in the fourth installment of The Mummy franchise, the first in nearly 20 years. Fraser’s Rick O'Connell and Rachel Weisz’s Evelyn Carnahan were already confirmed to bring the series’ jaunty, humorous action back to the silver screen, as was John Hannah as Carnahan’s brother.

The last of these casting announcements surfaced in March 2026; as of August, another big player is confirmed to re-join the crew, and he’s one with whom longtime fans will certainly be familiar.

Oded Fehr is making his grand return to The Mummy 4 as Ardeth Bay, who previously appeared in the original Mummy film as well as The Mummy Returns in 2001. He was notably absent from 2008’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, saying that without Imhotep as the big baddie, his character wouldn’t have any reason to appear.

It seems that Imhotep may have risen again, as Fehr has confirmed that he is involved in the new movie and even showed off a glimpse at what Ardeth Bay looks like eighteen years after the last film.

He shared the update in a post on his personal Instagram account on August 4, showing a clip of Ardeth in the original movie that then transitions to an image of fifty-five-year-old Fehr sitting in a makeup chair. Sporting a short haircut, a neat beard, and his signature facial tattoos, the now-silver Ardeth Bay looks as dashing as ever, and fans didn’t hesitate to express their excitement at his return.

Given his staunch dedication to Bay’s character and his refusal to return to the franchise if things didn’t make sense for him, it could be possible that Imhotep is also playing a significant role in the events of The Mummy 4. For now, its plot is still under wraps, but it has already received a release date for October 15, 2027.

Fraser has been tight-lipped about the events of the movie, fearing he might spoil things, but told audiences on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that he was “doing my best to get this 57-year-old gear in shape."

“I was hopeful for a long while, and then I was like, 'No, I don't know if they are,' you know. Other Mummy movies got made and…" he said of the project. "But anyway, look, what we're going to do is saddle back up, go back to the locations… I should probably stop talking like this because I don't want to give everything away."

Image Credits: Gerardo Mora/Getty Images

items.title: EA Acquisition by Saudi Arabia's PIF, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners Is Now Complete
items.description: EA has officially completed its $55 billion acquisition to an investor group comprised of Saudia Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
EA has officially completed its $55 billion acquisition to an investor group comprised of Saudia Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners.

Announced on August 4, 2026, this massive business move has been nearly one year in the making, first announced in September 2025.

"This moment recognizes the extraordinary people whose creativity, ambition and passion have made EA one of the world's leading interactive entertainment companies," Andrew Wilson, Chairman & CEO of Electronic Arts, said in a press release.

"We're entering this next chapter from a position of strength with partners who share our vision and ambition. Together, we'll invest boldly, accelerate innovation, and build the next generation of games and experiences for the hundreds of millions of players and fans who inspire us every day."

“Having been a minority investor in the company for more than five years, we have a deep understanding of EA’s unique platform, massive global sports and gaming franchises, and iconic IP,” Turqi Alnowaiser, Deputy Governor and Head of International Investments at PIF, added.

“Entertainment and sports are key areas of strategic focus for PIF, and are among the fastest growing and evolving sectors around the world. Together, the Consortium is uniquely positioned to be a long-term partner to EA’s management team in driving sustained growth and innovation for EA and the industry.”

As reported by The Financial Times after the acquisition was first announced in September 2025, the deal hinges on the hope that artificial intelligence will "significantly" cut EA's operating costs, helping the consortium of private investors to better manage the debt. Sources involved in the acquistions told the outlet that investors are betting these AI-spurred cuts will result in higher profits in the years to follow.

The use of AI in the gaming space has been a hot-button topic for some time now, with developers sharing conflicting opinions on the matter. Some, like Stranger Than Heaven director Masayoshi Yokoyama, says it might become inevitable in the creation of large-scale games in the vein of GTA 6 if demand for massive, open-world titles like it continues. Others, like Capcom, have said they will not use AI to create assets for its games, but will "proactively use it as a contributing technology to improve the efficiency and productivity of the game development process."

At the time of its announcement, EA's acquisition was the largest deal of its kind in history. Its official completion follows a hugely successful fiscal 2026 year, which, thanks to Battlefield 6's “highly successful launch," helped manage the company’s resilience in an “unpredictable external environment," earning its CEO an $8 million pay increase despite layoffs across the Battlefield teams.

items.title: Naoki Hamaguchi Doubles Down on Connecting All Final Fantasy VII Spin-Offs Into Revelation’s Ending
items.description: Final Fantasy VII Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi opened up on the game’s connection to the Advent Children film, saying that more than one of FF7’s spin-offs are going to tie into the game’s ending.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi opened up on the game’s connection to the Advent Children film, saying that more than one of FF7’s spin-offs are going to tie into the game’s ending.

In an interview with YouTuber Ashif’s Release Notes at Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival Berlin 2026, Naoki revealed that he’s well aware of the fan theories surrounding the next game in the Remake trilogy, particularly where ties to other properties in the FF7 universe are concerned.

He assured Ashif that he’s carefully considering all of these titles, specifically mentioning Dirge of Cerberus, Crisis Core, and of course, the Advent Children movie.

"I see a great deal of that discussion. I've seen a lot of people discussing and speculating off the back of interviews with myself and with Kitase-san, 'Is the ending of this going to connect to Advent Children?'” he began.

“But it's not a question. I don't want to sit here and say it connects to this, it connects to that. But obviously, there are a lot of other titles within the VII universe. So, we're talking about Advent Children, we're talking about Dirge of Cerberus, Crisis Core. And we want to bring all of those in and make sure we're not leaving those out.

“And then on top of that, once we have all of those in place, we're looking towards the ending. And then the question is, what kind of ending are we going to head for in Revelation that still has those ties? And I think that's something that I really hope players will look forward to finding out."

While Hamaguchi was careful not to say anything that would outright spoil things, his answer has certainly fueled an animated debate within the community, especially following similar comments previously made by other devs working on the Remake trilogy.

Hamaguchi made similar remarks in an August 1 interview with Automaton, confirming that the Remake series is a “new, overarching universe that encompasses the lore of the many various spin-offs” in the FF7 universe — “not just Advent Children, but also Dirge of Cerberus and Crisis Core.”

“We’re not denying the possibility of the ending tying into FFVII AC, but rather, we’re saying that FFVII AC has just been incorporated into the overarching FFVII remake series, including the ending. However, I won’t comment on whether the ending is positioned to lead into it,” he told the outlet.

And in 2023, producer Yoshinori Kitase told Eurogamer very definitely that this is the case: "We are finally going to link up with Advent Children, that is going to be part of canon," he said. "The overall storyline, the developments, will not go wildly out in a way that will not add up to Advent Children in the end. I don't think anyone wanted that, that's not what we're looking to create here.

"[But] to make sure it doesn't become stale and people know exactly where it's going, [that it] doesn't just follow the original word for word, we add in extra elements which add that little bit of doubt. Getting the right balance of that is so key. Ultimately, we're not trying to change the Final Fantasy 7 story into something really different. The overall balance wouldn't really allow for that anyway."

Hamaguchi’s latest comments have created stirred up a heated conversation within the fanbase, with some lamenting the trilogy’s shift away from the original game’s storyline in favor of a metaverse-style combo of all FF7 properties, while others remain cautiously optimistic about what this entails for the fates of Cloud, Tifa, Barret, and co.

In June, Hamaguchi spoke further about Revelation’s ending, saying that while players will be able to shape the story in some way, everyone will ultimately come to a "singular ending."

"The idea is to kind of change the approach and the depth of these story moments for these characters in this final chapter," he said. "We hope players look forward to that moment in the game."

Final Fantasy VII Revelation releases in spring 2027 on Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Loses Place in the Top 10 MCU Movies on Rotten Tomatoes Following Record-Breaking Opening
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is no longer among the top 10 highest-rated MCU films on Rotten Tomatoes.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is no longer among the top 10 highest-rated MCU films on Rotten Tomatoes.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is having a heck of a first week. The film has already broken multiple records, including having the biggest domestic opening weekend at the box office in history. The film dethroned Avengers: Endgame and has already racked up $1 billion at the box office, with an expectation that it will cross the $2 billion mark with ease. Its second weekend will be supported with a new IMAX release in North America, which will undoubtedly push people to rewatch the movie or give them another reason to see it for the first time.

However, amidst all of the records and success, the film has had a very small setback in one other area: Rotten Tomatoes. Of course, Rotten Tomatoes is hardly the be-all, end-all of a film, and some people don't care about the aggregate at all, but there's no denying that it's something the larger industry puts stock in when measuring a movie's critical success. As spotted by Forbes, Spider-Man: Brand New Day was in the top 10 highest-rated MCU flicks on Rotten Tomatoes up until this week, when its overall rating dropped to 89%.

Now, Brand New Day is tied with Captain America: The Winter Soldier and Civil War as the 11th highest-rated MCU film. Spider-Man's other MCU outings all place above it, with Homecoming in 6th place, Far From Home in 8th, and No Way Home in 5th place. This is bound to spark all kinds of discourse, as some feel Brand New Day is not only the best MCU Spidey movie but also one of the best iterations of the wall-crawler to ever hit the silver screen. Other fans have felt like Brand New Day loses some points for its villain, which isn't a traditional Spider-Man villain. So, maybe they'll agree with its placement.

items.title: Capcom Is Making a Life-Sized Leon Kennedy Statue for Resident Evil’s 30th Anniversary, and of Course the Internet Is Being Totally Normal About It
items.description: Capcom is preparing for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition in Shibuya, and to celebrate, it’s commissioning a life-sized statue of the beloved horror series’ poster boy, Leon S. Kennedy.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Leon Kennedy is coming to the real world… Well, sort of.

Capcom is preparing for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition in Shibuya, and to celebrate, it’s commissioning a life-sized statue of the beloved horror series’ poster boy, Leon S. Kennedy.

Kennedy will join the oodles of other life-sized Capcom character statues that decorate the company’s corporate offices and physical stores, alongside icons like Street Fighter’s Ryu charging up a hadouken and an adorable Palico from Monster Hunter Wilds.

As you can imagine, Resi fans are already going wild at the possibility of seeing Leon in the flesh (so to speak), and the posts that have resulted from Capcom’s announcement are… interesting, to say the least.

“I’m about to pull off a heist that they’re going to write about in textbooks for decades to come,” one player joked on X. (We get the feeling they weren’t actually joking, though.)

“That Leon statue is NOT going to be safe,” another remarked.

“You’re gonna need all the ‘Do Not Touch’ signs,” yet another warned.

I’m about to pull off a heist that they’re going to write about in textbooks for decades to come https://t.co/HYlezcrrvc

— dysi (@drexdqueen) August 3, 2026

The Resident Evil 30th Anniversary Exhibition will take place from October 30 to December 24, 2026 at the Shibuya BEAM Gallery, but tickets are already on sale as of August 3. A map of the exhibition has been released, though many of the activations therein are still labeled as ‘Coming Soon.’

The few that have been announced are Evidence of Horror, The World of Resident Evil Theater, and Memories of Those Who Stood Against Them, as well as the sale of exclusive promotional items.

Evidence of Horror has been described as a gallery featuring the iconic items and creatures from the Resident Evil franchise, which will include “life-sized models of villains crafted with meticulous detail,” as per SaigaNAK.

On the opposite end of the spectrum, Memories of Those Who Stood Against Them focuses on Resident Evil’s heroes and protagonists, following them from their first appearances to their latest interactions in the series’ most recent games. This is where Leon’s life-sized statue will be displayed.

And finally, The World of Resident Evil Theater will prepare attendees before they begin the exhibit, showing scenes from the series on a large screen, “enhancing immersion and excitement in the world of the story.”

Resident Evil is certainly having a moment lately, what with Requiem's staggering success and the Code Veronica Remake garnering over two million wishlists on Steam — not to mention the film adaptation (or rather, reimagining) of the series from the mind of Zach Cregger coming to theaters this September.

items.title: Microsoft Reportedly Planned to Continue Disc Support Before the Xbox 'Reset'
items.description: Digital Foundry's John Linneman says Microsoft planned to continue to support physical discs before the recent "reset" of the Xbox business, but it is unclear if the company will now do so with its next-gen console, Project Helix.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
UPDATE: We've updated this article to make it clear that Digital Foundry's John Linneman is speculating about what Microsoft may do in the future around physical discs, rather than reporting on the company's plans. Linneman did say his sources had indicated that Microsoft planned to continue to support physical discs before the recent "reset" of the Xbox business, but it is unclear if the company will now do so with its next-gen console, Project Helix.

ORIGINAL STORY: Digital Foundry's John Linneman says sources have told him that Microsoft is planning to continue support for physical game discs with the aim of prioritizing backward compatibility.

The topic came up during a Digital Foundry Q&A video posted to YouTube on July 31, where Linneman raised the optimistic possibility that discs might not be going the way of the dinosaur, at least on Xbox’s side of things.

However, the reason for this isn’t necessarily due to sales numbers; rather, Linneman says that backward compatibility is a bigger priority.

"I'd heard from a couple sort of sources — and this is just kind of like potential rumor-y stuff — but at least, before the current Xbox reset, I don't know where it is now, it sounds like Microsoft was actually very much going to continue disc support. Not because they value retail disc sales, but because they wanted to ensure that all your Xbox games were still playable on new Xboxes,” he explained.

He went on to envision a future where, in stark contrast to Sony’s future plans, Xbox doubles down on preserving physical media, even hinting at ties to Microsoft’s possible plans to digitize players’ physical game libraries.

"And it's like, 'We could offer maybe like an external drive,' or basically some means, and I think that might all tie into this disc-to-digital stuff, as well. But I get this feeling that they might actually, especially given their reaction — I'm not saying they're going to solve problems or anything drastically going to change — but I do see a future where Microsoft actually supports discs going forward, for users that want to take their library with them, while Sony just completely cuts people off."

While nothing has been officially confirmed by Xbox or Microsoft themselves, these reports come as welcome news to players in the wake of Sony’s hotly-debated decision to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028.

The company hasn’t backed down on this choice in spite of the massive backlash it’s received, either, with Sony’s Chief Financial Officer Lin Tao doubling down on killing discs in a first quarter fiscal results Q&A for investors in late July.

“We’re going to cautiously move this forward,” she said. “And to this decision, we have received various opinions and people have strong views, and we understand that the community has put forth those views to us. Games are loved by many people. It’s a form of entertainment that’s loved by people, and it’s connected to people’s fond memories in many cases.

“And so we understand those emotions. We want to consider that. And in the future digital ecosystem, how do we engage the gamers is something that we would like to continue to explore.”

Linneman’s latest comments follow optimistic remarks from Xbox’s Chief Technology Officer Scott Van Vliet following a network outage late last month. After hearing reports of players being unable to access their physical games during the outage, Vliet said that “disc-based entitlement checks should not prevent players from accessing their games, and this is by design,” something that set players’ minds at ease at least for a short while.

This is the latest Xbox news to stir up conversation among enthusiasts after a leaked document reportedly laid out plans to bring Xbox 360 games to both PC and its next-generation console, Project Helix, with a potential rollout slated for 2027-2028.

items.title: The RAM Crisis Seems to Be Expanding to Motherboards Now
items.description: According to a post on Board Channels, Motherboards will be going up in price during Q3 2026, making for yet another PC component to go up in price this year.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
So far, 2026 is no stranger to price increases. Since the calendar flipped over to the new year, RAM, graphics cards, SSDs and processors have all seen price jumps at the hands of AI, and now a leak suggests motherboards are next on the list.

Take this with a grain of salt, but according to a post on Board Channels, a Chinese tech forum known for industry leaks, and spotted by VideoCardz, prices for PCBs (printed circuit boards) will be going up by as much as 50% in Q3 2026. On top of the raw materials used in motherboards also going up, it seems like prices will see a major increase in the near future. The post also references the fact that the DIY market continues to weaken, which exacerbates the need for companies like MSI, Asus and Gigabyte to raise prices to make up for less volume.

It's not clear when these price increases will actually be reflected on store shelves. We are technically in Q3 right now, and the prices haven't gone up yet. In fact, just looking at the Asus ROG Strix X870E Gaming motherboard on Amazon, it seems like its price has actually gone down over the last year. However, it is just a post on Board Channels, so you should take it with a grain of salt regardless.

It's not surprising that the DIY market is shrinking, though. Due to the ongoing RAM crisis, pretty much every component that goes into a gaming PC has sharply increased in price, and now the prospect of building your own computer is a costly one.

If motherboards also go up in cost, the total price to build a PC is going to go up even more, as another step in PC gaming even more of a luxury hobby. After all, RAM has only continued to get more expensive since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest at the beginning of 2026. That crisis hasn't shown any signs of slowing down, either. Valve engineers have come out and said that prices are only getting worse, and even the Xbox Series X just got a price jump up to $799 for the 1TB model with a disk drive.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: 'Obviously It's Hugely Disappointing': Doctor Who Ex-Showrunner Says That Solving The Show's 'Knotty Problems' Will Take 'Time'
items.description: Solving the "problems" currently plaguing Doctor Who will take time, the series' former showrunner Chris Chibnall has cautioned, explaining that the show's most pressing issue now is "primarily about money."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Solving the "problems" currently plaguing Doctor Who will take time, the series' former showrunner Chris Chibnall has cautioned, explaining that the show's most pressing issue now is "primarily about money."

Doctor Who aired its final episode to date in May 2025, when lead actor Ncuti Gatwa departed the BBC's flagship sci-fi show after a largely disappointing couple of seasons. Co-funding partner Disney was formally confirmed as having ditched the series not long after, while the era's showrunner Russell T Davies announced he was done with the show back in June, when it was revealed that this year's previously-confirmed Christmas Special was actually not being made.

The BBC has said it will now offer the rights to make Doctor Who to other production companies but, some two months on, this has yet to happen. Indeed, it's unclear exactly what progress has been made on securing Doctor Who's future in general since the series went off-air over a year ago.

Now, speaking to the Who Corner to Corner podcast, the series' former head writer and showrunner Chris Chibnall has cautioned that "time" will be needed to fix the franchise — though suggested that money was "primarily" the reason it needed fixing in the first place.

"I think the biggest thing you can say about all of that is it's very easy to miss the point — that this is primarily about money," Chibnall said (thanks, Cultbox). "It's not really about all of the things that everybody is banging on about and moaning about or what or getting emotional about."

As a BBC-funded show, Doctor Who relies on money from the broadcasting company's public-backed budget — which has been cut in real terms over the past decade, while the costs and expectations of making big budget TV have only grown. This is the reason that the BBC partnered with Disney in the first place for the Ncuti Gatwa era, and why the company is now seeking a fresh co-production partner as a replacement.

"It's very hard for the BBC to fund their programs right now because of what's been done to them in terms of funding agreements over the past 15 years and the slow whittling away of that, and the increase in big Hollywood monoliths and conglomerates really taking over the market," Chibnall continued. "And really what you've got is [a situation where] the BBC can't afford to fully fund any drama now and it certainly can't afford to fund Doctor Who."

While funding has clearly been an issue for some time, many fans would likely point to the exit of previous funding partner Disney and suggest that the show is only in its current situation due to the creative decisions over the course of its most recent run that saw audience figures dwindle. (For our thoughts on the Ncuti Gatwa era, you can read our extensive set of episode reviews that offered the series a very mixed response.)

"There's all kinds of other things and obviously it's hugely disappointing and hasn’t been handled brilliantly," Chibnall said, seemingly eluding to the series' other issues. "But really, the big story is, look, this is a BBC that cannot afford to make shows that it wants to make. The BBC wants to make Doctor Who. Don't be in any doubt about that."

A recent report that cited other TV insiders claimed that Doctor Who is now unlikely to return on-screen for up to five years while the series' production is rebuilt from the ground up. The simplest route forward for the show would likely be if BBC Studios, the BBC's separate commercial arm, won the rights to produce the series. But even this requires the co-production company search to begin — and so far, there's been no sign of this.

"There are lots of things they will have to have to sort out," Chibnall concluded. "And I guess the byproduct of the Disney deal ending is you had a funder and then that funder is now gone and it’s hard," Chibnall concluded. "It will take some on any show it would take some work to then convince other co-production partners to come in at that point when somebody else has dropped out.

"So like I say, it all reverts back to money and those are knotty problems that do take time. And in an ideal world, it wouldn’t come off air while you're sorting that stuff."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: 'It Would Be a Real Shame for That Culture to Disappear': Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Director Says Physical Game Releases Must Continue
items.description: Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi has said that the end of physical games risked part of our culture disappearing, in the wake of Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi has said that the end of physical games risked part of our culture disappearing, in the wake of Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs.

Last month, Sony made headlines when it announced and end to new games shipping on disc from January 2028 onwards, triggering a huge backlash from many fans. Now, at the recent FF14 Fan Fest, Ashif’s Release Notes asked Hamaguchi for his personal thoughts on the matter.

"In terms of my thoughts on physical editions, as a gamer myself, I love them," Hamaguchi replied, adding that, as a game creator, it made him happy when fans asked him to sign their physical copies.

"It would be a real shame for that culture to disappear," Hamaguchi continued. "I think physical games will still be sold in some form in the future, for example as a download code in a box. Moreover, I want physical games to continue — both as a creator and a game fan."

This isn't the first time that Hamaguchi has addressed the end of physical games. At the same event, the director said he was pushing for a physical release for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, though admitted that the matter had not yet been decided.

The long-awaited final part of FF7's remake trilogy, Revelation is currently slated for a spring 2027 release, when it will also launch across multiple platforms simultaneously. Asked again about a physical launch for the title, Hamaguchi reiterated that he would "like to have some kind of physical edition available," though could not yet make any promises. "We are looking into what the best options are, but I hope we will be able to live up to your expectations," he added.

"As it's nearing completion, I can personally pick it up and say, 'this feels good, this feels satisfying'," Hamaguchi said of the game in general, "so I’m quite confident about it. Of course, the final judgement will be down to the players but I feel confident, I can see the end, and I can finally feel the pressure lifting."

Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth started out as PlayStation exclusives before being released on other platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2. However, FF7 Revelation is due to ship on PC, PS5, Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S simultaneously — a first for the remake trilogy.

"For me, it is quite meaningful to be able to bring it back to Nintendo platforms," Hamaguchi said of Revelation's multi-platform launch. A self-confessed FF6 fan, Hamaguchi recalled witnessing Final Fantasy's move from Nintendo to PlayStation as a child, and remembers playing the original FF7 on PS1, when the series moved from SNES cartridges to the greater possibilities offered by Sony’s compact disc format.

Other Japanese game creators have also given their opinions on physical games and the all-digital future we seem to be heading towards. Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa addressed Sony’s decision directly, saying that although it made sense from a business perspective Sony “may never have considered what physical editions mean to the people who value them." Hideo Kojima said of Sony’s decision that "I grew up with physical media, so I find it really sad." Nier creator Yoko Taro also echoed these sentiments in an X post where he encouraged people to buy physical game releases while they still can.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi has said that the end of physical games risked part of our culture disappearing, in the wake of Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs.

Last month, Sony made headlines when it announced and end to new games shipping on disc from January 2028 onwards, triggering a huge backlash from many fans. Now, at the recent FF14 Fan Fest, Ashif’s Release Notes asked Hamaguchi for his personal thoughts on the matter.

"In terms of my thoughts on physical editions, as a gamer myself, I love them," Hamaguchi replied, adding that, as a game creator, it made him happy when fans asked him to sign their physical copies.

"It would be a real shame for that culture to disappear," Hamaguchi continued. "I think physical games will still be sold in some form in the future, for example as a download code in a box. Moreover, I want physical games to continue — both as a creator and a game fan."

This isn't the first time that Hamaguchi has addressed the end of physical games. At the same event, the director said he was pushing for a physical release for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, though admitted that the matter had not yet been decided.

The long-awaited final part of FF7's remake trilogy, Revelation is currently slated for a spring 2027 release, when it will also launch across multiple platforms simultaneously. Asked again about a physical launch for the title, Hamaguchi reiterated that he would "like to have some kind of physical edition available," though could not yet make any promises. "We are looking into what the best options are, but I hope we will be able to live up to your expectations," he added.

"As it's nearing completion, I can personally pick it up and say, 'this feels good, this feels satisfying'," Hamaguchi said of the game in general, "so I’m quite confident about it. Of course, the final judgement will be down to the players but I feel confident, I can see the end, and I can finally feel the pressure lifting."

Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth started out as PlayStation exclusives before being released on other platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2. However, FF7 Revelation is due to ship on PC, PS5, Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S simultaneously — a first for the remake trilogy.

"For me, it is quite meaningful to be able to bring it back to Nintendo platforms," Hamaguchi said of Revelation's multi-platform launch. A self-confessed FF6 fan, Hamaguchi recalled witnessing Final Fantasy's move from Nintendo to PlayStation as a child, and remembers playing the original FF7 on PS1, when the series moved from SNES cartridges to the greater possibilities offered by Sony’s compact disc format.

Other Japanese game creators have also given their opinions on physical games and the all-digital future we seem to be heading towards. Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa addressed Sony’s decision directly, saying that although it made sense from a business perspective Sony “may never have considered what physical editions mean to the people who value them." Hideo Kojima said of Sony’s decision that "I grew up with physical media, so I find it really sad." Nier creator Yoko Taro also echoed these sentiments in an X post where he encouraged people to buy physical game releases while they still can.
